Edinburgh is a thriving area with strong demand for reliable boiler repair and servicing services. Local properties range from period Victorian and Edwardian homes through to modern new-build developments, each presenting different plumbing requirements and challenges.

Our Gas Safe registered engineers serve all areas of Edinburgh and the surrounding City of Edinburgh region. Whether you're in the town centre or the surrounding residential areas, we provide prompt, professional boiler repair services with transparent pricing and no hidden call-out charges.

With years of experience working across City of Edinburgh, our engineers understand the specific plumbing challenges faced by local homeowners. From the older pipe infrastructure common in period properties to the modern systems found in newer developments, our team has the expertise to handle any boiler repair and servicing requirement.

We cover all postcodes across Edinburgh with same-day availability for urgent work. All our engineers are fully qualified, insured, and committed to leaving your property clean and tidy after every job.

faqs.q: How do I know if my boiler needs repairing or replacing?
faqs.a: If your boiler is under 10 years old and the repair cost is less than £400, repair is usually better value. Over 10 years old or repair costs exceeding 50% of a new boiler — consider replacement.

faqs.q: Why does my boiler keep losing pressure?
faqs.a: Pressure loss is usually caused by a small leak in the system, a faulty pressure relief valve, or a failing expansion vessel. A Gas Safe engineer can diagnose and fix the root cause — simply topping up the pressure is a temporary fix.

faqs.q: My boiler is making a banging noise — what does it mean?
faqs.a: Banging, kettling, or clunking sounds usually indicate limescale buildup on the heat exchanger, a failing pump, or trapped air in the system. All are repairable by a qualified engineer.

faqs.q: How long does a boiler repair take?
faqs.a: Most boiler repairs take 1-3 hours. If specialist parts need ordering, the initial visit diagnoses the fault and the repair is completed on a second visit typically within 24-48 hours.

localParagraph: Edinburgh's mix of Georgian townhouses in the New Town, Victorian tenements across Leith and Marchmont, and modern developments around the waterfront means boiler repair engineers here need to be genuinely versatile, working comfortably across a wide range of heating system ages and configurations. The city's mixed water hardness presents an additional consideration — while not as aggressively hard as parts of southern England, Edinburgh homes can still experience gradual limescale accumulation in heat exchangers and pipework, which often contributes to reduced efficiency and eventual breakdowns if systems aren't periodically serviced. Older properties with original pipework, particularly in tenement flats along Dalry Road or Gorgie, may also present more complex fault-finding challenges than newer builds. When choosing a boiler repair specialist in Edinburgh, it's worth confirming they hold Gas Safe registration, carry common replacement parts, and have relevant experience with the property type you own — whether that's a sandstone period conversion or a purpose-built modern flat — to ensure the work is completed correctly the first time.
whatItInvolves: Boiler repair covers fault diagnosis and component replacement to restore a failing or broken boiler to full working order. Common faults include pressure loss, ignition failure, pump failure, heat exchanger leaks, PCB failure, and faulty diverter valves. A qualified Gas Safe engineer will identify the root cause — not just reset the fault code.
process: The engineer connects a diagnostic reader to your boiler's PCB to extract fault codes, then conducts a systematic inspection of the key components: heat exchanger, pump, igniter, gas valve, pressure relief valve, and expansion vessel. Once the fault is identified you'll receive a fixed repair quote. Parts are ordered and fitted on the same visit where possible, or next-day for specialist components.
whatToExpect: Most boiler repairs are completed in 1-3 hours. Always ask for a written report of the fault and the work carried out — you'll need this if the boiler fails again under guarantee. If the repair cost exceeds 50% of a new boiler's value, a replacement is usually better value long-term.
